results.problem: Approximate sorting with persistent random comparison faults
results.bound: $O(n \log n)$ time, $O(\log n)$ maximum dislocation, $O(n)$ total dislocation w.h.p. for $p < 1/4$
results.quote: RiffleSort is a randomized algorithm that approximately sorts S in O(n log n) worst-case time. The maximum dislocation and the total dislocation of the returned sequence are at most O(log n) and at most O(n), respectively, with probability at least 1 - O(log n / (n sqrt n)).

results.problem: Approximate rank estimation in persistent error model
results.bound: $O(\log m)$ time, rank estimate within $O(d)$ of true rank w.h.p.
results.quote: NoisySearch(S,x,d) that runs in O(log m) worst-case time and returns an index τ_x ∈ [rank(x,S) - αd, rank(x,S) + αd] with probability at least 1 - O(m^-6), where α ≥ 2 is a constant that depends only on p.

results.bound: $O(m w_S)$ time, $O(\log m)$ maximum dislocation, $O(m)$ total dislocation w.h.p.
results.quote: BasketSort(S,w_S) is a deterministic algorithm that approximately sorts S in O(m w_S) worst-case time. The maximum dislocation and the total dislocation of the returned sequence are at most β_max · lnm and β_tot · m, respectively, with probability 1 - O(m^-3), where β_max ≥ 2 and β_tot are constants that come from Lemma 5.12 and Lemma 5.19, respectively, and depend only on p and q.

results.problem: Approximate sorting with persistent random comparison faults
results.bound: $\Omega(\log n)$ maximum dislocation lower bound w.h.p.
results.quote: No (possibly randomized) algorithm can achieve maximum dislocation o(log n) with high probability.

results.problem: Approximate sorting with persistent random comparison faults
results.quote: No (possibly randomized) algorithm can achieve an expected total dislocation of o(n).

results.problem: Approximate sorting with persistent random comparison faults (deterministic)
results.bound: $O(n \log n)$ time, $O(\log n)$ maximum dislocation, $O(n)$ total dislocation w.h.p., deterministic
results.quote: There exists a deterministic algorithm that approximately sorts S in O(n log n) worst-case time. The maximum dislocation and the total dislocation of the returned sequence are at most O(log n) and at most O(n), respectively, with high probability.
